London Taverns

Thomas Heywood (c. 1570–1641)

T
HE
 G
ENTRY
 to the 
King’s Head,
The Nobles to the 
Crown,
The Knights unto the 
Golden Fleece,
And to the 
Plough,
 the Clown.
The Churchman to the 
Mitre,
The Shepherd to the 
Star,
The Gardener hies him to the 
Rose,
To the 
Drum,
 the man of war.
To the 
Feathers,
 Ladies you! The 
Globe,
The Seaman doth not scorn!
The Usurer to the 
Devil;
 and
The Townsman to the 
Horn.
The Huntsman to the 
White Hart,
To the 
Ship,
 the Merchant goes;
But you that do the Muses love,
The 
Swan,
 called river Po.
The Bankrupt to the 
World’s End,
The Fool to the 
Fortune
 hie;
Unto the 
Mouth,
 the Oyster Wife;
The Fidler to the 
Pie….
